# Prepare data

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sccomp)

# sccomp_boxplot will call internal function which will check the cache directory, 
# so we need to set the cache directory before calling sccomp_boxplot.
utils::assignInNamespace("sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir", cache_stan_model_dir, ns="sccomp")

# BayesPrism fractions: RNA.ID + one column per cell type (what 10 reads)
prop_table=fread("fileList1.txt", header=FALSE)
fraction_name=prop_table$V2[1]
fraction_file=prop_table$V1[1]
prefix=fraction_name

meta_table=fread("fileList3.txt", header=FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(V3 == fraction_name) |>
  dplyr::select(-V3) 
meta_options=split(meta_table$V1, meta_table$V2)
sample_col=meta_options$sample_col
condition_col=meta_options$condition_col
condition_control=meta_options$condition_control
meta=fread(meta_options$filepath, header=TRUE, data.table=FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c(sample_col, condition_col) %in% colnames(meta)))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
prop_wide <- fread(fraction_file, data.table=FALSE)
stopifnot(all(prop_wide$RNA.ID %in% meta[[sample_col]]))
print_table(prop_wide, byDT=TRUE, row.names=FALSE)
prop_long = prop_wide |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols=-RNA.ID, names_to="cell_group", values_to="abundance") |>
  dplyr::left_join(meta, by=setNames(sample_col, "RNA.ID")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    sample=RNA.ID,
    type=!!sym(condition_col)
  )  

stopifnot(condition_control %in% prop_long$type)
condition_levels=unique(as.character(prop_long$type))
condition_levels=c(condition_control, as.character(condition_levels[condition_levels != condition_control]))
prop_long$type=factor(prop_long$type, levels=condition_levels)
```

inference_method `r inference_method` is used for sccomp_estimate.

```{r results='hide'}
all_estimate = sccomp_estimate( 
  prop_long,
  formula_composition = ~type, # we want to use contrasts, so no intercept
  sample = "sample", 
  cell_group = "cell_group",
  abundance  = "abundance",
  bimodal_mean_variability_association = FALSE,
  inference_method = inference_method,
  verbose = FALSE,
  cores = cores,
  cache_stan_model = normalizePath(cache_stan_model_dir)
) 
```

# About removing outliers

sccomp can identify outliers probabilistically and exclude them from the estimation. 
However, it might not work for this project. Here, we provide the result with and without 
removing outliers. Please look at the result and decide which one represents your experimental 
design.

# Without removing outliers

```{r}
cur_estiate=all_estimate
cur_prefix=paste0(prefix, ".notRemovingOutliers")
```

```{r child="sccomp_sub.rmd"}
```

# With removing outliers

After running sccomp_estimate, we will run sccomp_remove_outliers before sccomp_test.

```{r results="hide"}
cur_estiate = all_estimate |>
  sccomp_remove_outliers(max_sampling_iterations = 2000, verbose=FALSE)
cur_prefix=paste0(prefix, ".removingOutliers")
```

```{r child="sccomp_sub.rmd"}
```
